fields.summary: Autonomous plan run for change set Workflow authoring; no owner took part. The planner read the change set's intent, the workflows area, the landed decisions explain-custom-workflows, workflow-writing-tools and built-in-workflows-by-name, and internal/api/run.go (resolveWorkflow, workflowResolver), which today resolve a bare name to the repo's .rhiza/workflows/<name>.toml, else the built-in. It carved workflow-authoring and workflow-overrides out of Area workflows. Four questions went to the arbiter in one batch: which intent the change set serves, whether to add a personal (user-level) override layer, what workflow describe shows, and how workflow new behaves. The arbiter's Decision workflow-authoring-shape settled them: serve power-users-first; add the personal layer with order personal ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/rhiza/workflows, else ~/.config/rhiza/workflows), then repo, then built-in, shared by run start, workflow steps, ls, describe and check; describe shows the resolved source, the layers it shadows and the steps with kinds, targets, roles and includes, read-only, with --json; new writes .rhiza/workflows/<name>.toml from --from <workflow> or a commented skeleton, bare names only, refusing an existing file with exit 3 and validating as check does. The planner then wrote leaves: workflow ls, describe, new, check and a guide topic under workflow-authoring, and workflow-overrides as the personal-layer leaf. Nothing was left open.
fields.title: Plan interview: workflow authoring (autonomous)
